contracts.commit_point: The httpx request hook raising MCPEgressBlocked before bytes leave, fired once per hop including redirect targets (mcp.py:104-114); build-time refusal of the configured endpoint at mcp.py:459-464.
contracts.declared_mechanism: _network_block_reason classifies the configured endpoint host at build time and build_client omits refused servers (mcp.py:65-87, 459-464); _egress_httpx_client_factory appends _egress_request_hook to every httpx client's request event hooks, failing closed if the SDK helper moves (mcp.py:119-157, 465-477); the hook re-classifies request.url.host per hop via classify_host — the shared single source of truth (guard.py:303-318) — and raises MCPEgressBlocked (mcp.py:89-116).
contracts.forbidden_condition: An MCP client request reaching a host explicitly denied by permissions.network or not present on its non-empty allowlist — including a 3xx redirect from an allow-listed endpoint to a denied host.
pending_binding_information: The controller/MCP-refresh call sites that construct the NetworkPolicy and pass it to load_mcp_tools/build_client are not in the supplied views.
contracts.protected_operation: Outgoing HTTP requests to MCP server endpoints (the transport for mcp__ agent tool calls; also prompt/resource fetches over the same client).
contracts.protected_resource: The permissions.network per-host egress allow/deny policy as applied to MCP endpoints.
contracts.protection_obligation: MCP HTTP/SSE (streamable_http) egress must be gated by the permissions.network policy: a connection to a host that is denied or not on the allowlist must be refused at client build, and every outgoing request — including each redirect hop — must raise MCPEgressBlocked before any bytes leave, via the httpx request hook.
scope_limits: stdio MCP servers have no egress host and are never blocked here (mcp.py:74-77); an empty/inert policy leaves behavior unchanged.
The per-request factory is attached only to streamable_http/sse connections (mcp.py:472-477); websocket endpoints get the build-time host check but no per-request hook in the supplied code.
The hook covers all traffic on the MCP client (prompts, resources), not only agent tool invocations; the agent-tool path is the asserted mediation.

contracts.commit_point: The LangGraph resume in SessionDriver._stream_turn after the engine decision is produced — the network tool executes only on resume with the decision payload (session.py:1025-1041).
contracts.declared_mechanism: build_runtime collects every non-identity-ungated tool name and calls interrupt_map(extra_gated, include_async=...) so web/MCP/async-subagent tools map to ActionKind.NETWORK and are gated (runtime.py:778-798); tool_to_action falls through unknown and mcp__-prefixed names to NETWORK with a diagnostic for unknown tools (permissions_bridge.py:184-195); MCP namespacing to mcp__<server>__<tool> preserves classification soundness (mcp.py:289-312, 557-560).
contracts.forbidden_condition: A web/MCP/async-subagent tool call issuing its network request without engine evaluation — e.g., an mcp__-prefixed or unknown tool silently inheriting a permissive classification, or an extra tool bypassing the gated path.
pending_binding_information: jarn.agent.web_tools.build_web_tools is not supplied; the exact web tool set is inferred from permissions_bridge/engine references.
The loader path from load_mcp_tools results into build_runtime's extra_tools argument (controller call site) is not in the supplied views.
contracts.protected_operation: Invocation of network-classified extra agent tools (web_search, web_fetch, mcp__* tools, ASYNC_SUBAGENT_TOOLS).
contracts.protected_resource: Outbound network endpoints reached through those agent tools (web targets, MCP servers, Agent-Protocol deployments).
contracts.protection_obligation: Every network-capable extra tool call — builtin web tools (web_search/web_fetch), MCP-loaded tools (mcp__<server>__<tool>), and the async-subagent tools when configured — must be registered in the deepagents interrupt map and pass a permission-engine decision before the network request is made; un-namespaced extras cannot bypass the engine.
scope_limits: Locally built read-only extras (wiki_search/wiki_read, repo_map, background controls) are deliberately excluded from gating by object identity (runtime.py:783-793).
This contract covers pre-exec tool gating only; MCP transport-level egress policy enforcement is a separate contract.
spawn_parallel_tasks and the task tool are added after/outside the interrupt map by design (runtime.py:863-900); their internal subagent gating is not asserted here.

contracts.commit_point: The approver invocation when an ASK reaches driver.approver during interrupt resolution — the raise converts the decision into a refusal before any resume payload is produced (interrupts.py:229-234 invoking the approver; headless.py:475-479 raising).
contracts.declared_mechanism: _make_fail_closed_approver returns an Approver whose callback raises HeadlessRefusal for every ASK reaching it (headless.py:464-481); _run_headless wires it as the session approver via run_agent_turn(approver=approver) (headless.py:589-590, 643-650); HeadlessRefusal carries kind='refusal' and exit_code=EXIT_PERMISSION_DENIED (headless.py:112-125); a second layer raises HeadlessRefusal on rejected/blocked/auto-denied approval events (headless.py:628-639).
contracts.forbidden_condition: A gated tool's ASK decision being satisfied without a human in a headless run (silent auto-approval), allowing the tool to execute unattended.
pending_binding_information: jarn.agent.turn_runner.run_agent_turn is not supplied; the hand-off of the approver into the SessionDriver is known only via the call site.
contracts.protected_operation: The approval decision for gated agent tool actions in headless turns.
contracts.protected_resource: The Approver callback slot / approval gate in the headless turn pipeline.
contracts.protection_obligation: In headless (non-interactive) mode, any gated action that reaches an ASK approval decision must be refused — the fail-closed approver raises HeadlessRefusal (exit kind refusal / EXIT_PERMISSION_DENIED) — so no gated tool is approved or executed without a human; unattended execution requires explicit auto-edit/yolo opt-in.
scope_limits: Auto-approving modes (auto-edit/yolo) resolve most actions to ALLOW before the approver; the fail-closed approver still denies any residual ASK such as danger-guard DANGEROUS (headless.py:466-473).
The interactive REPL approver is a different wiring and out of scope; only the headless approver is asserted.
The approval verdict itself is the guarded state transition; the strata of tools that would have executed downstream are covered by the gating contracts.

contracts.commit_point: The middleware wrapping of tool execution in the compiled graph — create_deep_agent(middleware=[read_filter_mw]) — where sensitive hits are stripped from results before the model sees them (runtime.py:929-939).
contracts.declared_mechanism: ReadResultFilterMiddleware bound to the session's authoritative PermissionEngine is injected on the main agent and every jarn-built subagent spec (runtime.py:902-921, 293-328); the engine predicate read_content_blocked leads with the secret-store check, then deny rules, then allow, then sensitive globs — an allow rule can never unlock the store (engine.py:329-351); the same engine instance receives runtime deny_session/remember so session denials are honored by the filter (runtime.py:264-290).
contracts.forbidden_condition: A broad read tool result containing secret-store (or denied/sensitive) file contents reaching the model because the pre-exec gate judged only the benign search scope.
pending_binding_information: jarn.agent.read_filter.ReadResultFilterMiddleware source is not in the supplied views; the filtering behavior is characterized by runtime wiring/docstrings and the engine predicate only (drop vs. redact semantics unverified).
contracts.protected_operation: Post-execution filtering of read tool results before they enter model-visible session context.
contracts.protected_resource: Secret-store file contents (and generally contents of read-denied/sensitive paths).
contracts.protection_obligation: Broad-read tool results (grep/glob-style content searches) must be filtered so contents of jarn's secret store — and other denied/sensitive paths — are never surfaced to the model, even when the pre-exec gate auto-allowed the benign search scope.
scope_limits: The guarded effect is content entering model-visible session state; the filesystem read itself is not mutated by this contract.
Remote out-of-process async subagents are out of scope — their reads are the remote harness's concern (runtime.py:313-316, 915-916).

contracts.commit_point: The DENY verdict consumed in resolve_interrupts — the reject decision is yielded and the gated tool is never resumed (interrupts.py:223-228).
contracts.declared_mechanism: evaluate() checks _touches_secret_store immediately after the danger-guard BLOCKED tier and before deny rules, allow rules, and any mode, returning the fixed _SECRET_STORE_DENIAL with dangerous=True and block_remember_always=True (engine.py:155-164, 207-220); _touches_secret_store judges READ over every candidate (target plus grep/glob read_targets) and WRITE on its target (engine.py:371-398); _is_secret_store_path binds the store by resolved-identity within secret_store_dirs and by casefolded lexical globs, widening with resolved symlinks (engine.py:400-435).
contracts.forbidden_condition: A READ or WRITE tool action whose target — or any grep/glob read candidate — resolves into the secret store being allowed by an allow rule, session approval, or coarse mode; or such an action being remembered as a persisted ALWAYS rule.
pending_binding_information: The concrete store directory list and glob patterns (engine.py:69-72) cannot be verified from the redacted source.
contracts.protected_operation: Path-addressed read/write tool actions evaluated by PermissionEngine.evaluate (actions derived from gated agent tool calls).
contracts.protection_obligation: Agent path-addressed READ/WRITE tool actions touching jarn's own secret store (~/.jarn/secrets/<service>/<account> under $JARN_HOME, plus project-level .jarn/secrets) must be hard-denied above the allow tier: un-allowlistable, never persisted as a remembered rule, and unreachable in any permission mode including yolo.
scope_limits: SHELL and NETWORK actions are out of scope for _touches_secret_store; shell access to the store is covered by a separate danger-guard contract.
The store path constants and lexical globs are redacted in the supplied view; identity matching relies on jarn.config.paths.secret_store_dirs, which is referenced but not supplied.

contracts.commit_point: The LangGraph resume in SessionDriver._stream_turn — the mutation gate explicitly covers SHELL-gated run_in_background starts alongside write_file/edit_file/execute (session.py:1027-1041).
contracts.declared_mechanism: MUTATING_TOOLS includes execute (permissions_bridge.py:20-21); run_in_background is gated exactly like execute as a SHELL action (permissions_bridge.py:98-103, 138-140); the interrupt map plus engine.evaluate in resolve_interrupts must resolve approve/reject/edit before resume (interrupts.py:215-264).
contracts.forbidden_condition: A shell command (foreground execute or a background-process start) executing without a permission-engine decision on the SHELL action carrying that command.
pending_binding_information: The execution backend implementation that ultimately spawns the process (jarn backends factory) is not in the supplied views.
contracts.protected_operation: Execution of the execute tool and run_in_background starts, mapped to ActionKind.SHELL with the command string as target.
contracts.protected_resource: The host OS process/shell surface the execution backend runs commands on.
contracts.protection_obligation: Every shell-executing agent tool call — the execute tool and run_in_background starts — must be registered in the deepagents interrupt map and pass a permission-engine decision (SHELL-classified, command inspected) before the command runs.
scope_limits: Background control tools (check/kill/list_background) are intentionally ungated as read-only controls of agent-started processes (permissions_bridge.py:98-103).
Pattern-based guarding only; OS/docker sandbox enforcement is a separate layer not asserted by this contract.

contracts.commit_point: The drop in build_runtime's kept-list loop, executed before create_deep_agent is called (runtime.py:691-708, then 929-939).
contracts.declared_mechanism: _RESERVED_BUILTIN_NAMES collects every builtin tool name (runtime.py:82-106); the assembly loop drops any extra tool (identified by the pre-wiring object-identity set _extra_ids) whose name is un-prefixed and reserved, warning instead of raising (runtime.py:691-708); the MCP loader complements this by stamping mcp__<server>__<tool> provenance on every tool before it leaves the loader (mcp.py:289-312, 557-560).
contracts.forbidden_condition: An un-namespaced extra tool carrying a reserved builtin name surviving into create_deep_agent's tool list, where tool_to_action would treat it as a (read-only) builtin and the engine would auto-ALLOW it in every mode including plan — letting a networked/mutating tool run without approval.
pending_binding_information: The deepagents-side handling of the tools list after create_deep_agent is external and not supplied.
contracts.protected_operation: Agent tool registration/assembly in build_runtime — the construction of the tool list handed to create_deep_agent.
contracts.protected_resource: The reserved builtin tool names / the tool-name namespace that permission classification is keyed on.
contracts.protection_obligation: An un-namespaced extra tool (web/MCP-provided) whose name collides with a reserved jarn builtin name must be dropped at agent assembly, so it can never be registered under a name that name-keyed permission classification would misclassify and auto-allow.
scope_limits: The affected state is the assembled agent tool registry; the drop happens at startup assembly, before any agent turn.

web_search/web_fetch are deliberately not reserved (they are jarn's own NETWORK-mapped tools and stay gated); identity-based un-gating of locally built read-only tools is unaffected (runtime.py:787-793).
Genuine builtins and correctly namespaced mcp__ tools are never dropped.

contracts.commit_point: handle_update's early return on a rejected decision, before any dispatch — backend.submit_verdict (bot.py:499-553) and backend.submit_turn (bot.py:680-685) are reachable only after authorization.
contracts.declared_mechanism: handle_update invokes authorize_update(update, self.allowed_user_ids) first and returns (logging the reason) on any not ok decision before callback or message handling (bot.py:434-444); authorize_update enforces not_private / no_principal / not_allowed with an empty allowlist denying everyone (auth.py:103-122); principal extraction fails closed (auth.py:46-72); gateway startup refuses to boot with an empty allowlist (cli.py:215-231).
contracts.forbidden_condition: An update from a non-private chat, an update with no extractable principal (including missing 'from' on a present envelope, never falling back to chat.id), or a sender not in allowed_user_ids reaching backend.submit_turn / backend.submit_verdict.
pending_binding_information: GatewayBackend.submit_turn/submit_verdict implementations (jarn.telegram.backend) are not in the supplied views; downstream handling of an authorized dispatch is characterized only by these call sites.
contracts.protected_operation: Dispatch of authorized inbound Telegram updates to the gateway backend (submit_turn for turns; submit_verdict for approval verdicts).
contracts.protected_resource: The gateway backend / agent-session control channel reached through the Telegram transport.
contracts.protection_obligation: Every inbound Telegram update must pass a deny-by-default, DM-only allowlist authorization — private chat, non-null from.id principal extracted fail-closed, sender id in allowed_user_ids, empty allowlist admits nobody — in TelegramBotApp.handle_update before the update may be dispatched to the gateway backend as a turn or an approval verdict.
scope_limits: Applies to the Telegram long-poll transport's handle_update dispatch path; startup backlog updates are fetched, reported verbatim, and never executed (bot.py:172-232).

The turn-submission path is operator-initiated input that starts agent turns; the lifecycle binding rests on the approval-verdict path, which resolves the agent's HITL approval cards (tool/plan/memory/skill kinds).

contracts.commit_point: The resulting DENY verdict consumed in resolve_interrupts — the reject decision prevents the shell tool from resuming (interrupts.py:223-228).
contracts.declared_mechanism: inspect_command returns GuardLevel.BLOCKED on a _JARN_SECRET_PATH match, before the rm/network/rule scans (guard.py:63-71, 402-416); engine._guard_for threads SHELL actions through inspect_command (engine.py:462-466), and BLOCKED maps to an un-allowlistable DENY at the top of evaluate's precedence (engine.py:213-217).
contracts.forbidden_condition: A shell command matching the jarn secret-store path pattern (absolute, tilde, or environment spellings) executing — e.g., cat/sed-style reads of the store in full-access mode.
pending_binding_information: The literal store-path regex is redacted in the supplied view; only its documented match classes (absolute/tilde/env spellings) are verifiable.
contracts.protected_operation: Shell command execution via SHELL-classified agent tool actions.
contracts.protected_resource: The jarn credential store, accessed via shell commands.
contracts.protection_obligation: Shell commands (execute / run_in_background) whose text names jarn's own credential store must be hard-blocked by the danger-guard — refused outright above modes and allowlists — so shell access cannot bypass the path-aware tool bridge.
scope_limits: The guard is a pattern-based net, not a sandbox; obfuscated equivalents are an acknowledged residual (guard.py:7-19).
Other credential-bearing paths (.env, .ssh, .aws/credentials, *.pem/*.key) route to DANGEROUS (confirm), not BLOCKED — out of this contract's hard-deny scope.

contracts.commit_point: The LangGraph resume in SessionDriver._stream_turn: ordinary reads resume silently on ALLOW (interrupts.py:217-222); sensitive/denied reads surface through the approver or reject path before the tool resumes (session.py:1027-1041).
contracts.declared_mechanism: READONLY_TOOLS are registered in the interrupt map in every mode so reads reach the engine (permissions_bridge.py:43-49, 62-76); tool_to_action builds READ actions whose read_targets capture both the search path and the file glob (permissions_bridge.py:146-170); the engine's _read_decision returns ASK when any candidate is sensitive and not cleared by an allow matching that same candidate (engine.py:233-260).
contracts.forbidden_condition: A read of a sensitive path (or one matching a read-deny rule) executing without engine inspection — e.g., a grep whose glob narrows onto .env/id_rsa/.aws/credentials auto-allowing on a benign search scope, or a user's permissions.deny on a path being dead because reads never reach the engine.
pending_binding_information: The engine's sensitive-glob default list (DEFAULT_SENSITIVE_READ_GLOBS) is visible, but per-session rule resolution from config into PermissionEngine.rules is characterized only by type hints.
contracts.protected_operation: Execution of gated read tool calls (read_file/ls/glob/grep), judged per candidate target (path plus glob).
contracts.protected_resource: Sensitive files on the filesystem (paths matched by permissions.sensitive_read_globs or read-deny rules).
contracts.protection_obligation: Read tool calls (read_file, ls, glob, grep) must be routed through the permission engine so their path and file-glob targets are inspected against sensitive-read globs and read-deny rules — a sensitive-path read must ASK (or be denied) rather than silently auto-allowing — before the read executes and its content is surfaced to the model.
scope_limits: The gated effect is a filesystem read, not a mutation; the stratum denotes the filesystem access at the resume commit, and the harm addressed is sensitive-content disclosure.
Gating adds no prompt for ordinary reads — the engine auto-ALLOWs them and interrupts resumes ALLOW silently (permissions_bridge.py:43-48, interrupts.py:217-222).
Post-execution content filtering for broad searches is a separate contract; this contract asserts only pre-exec routing and per-candidate judgment.

contracts.commit_point: The LangGraph resume in SessionDriver._stream_turn: the gated tool executes only when the graph is resumed at the top of the loop with the decision payload; the mutation gate at session.py:1041 guarantees the pre-mutation ordering on every resolution path.
contracts.declared_mechanism: interrupt_map() registers MUTATING_TOOLS (plus wiki-mutating extras) in the interrupt_on dict for create_deep_agent in every mode (permissions_bridge.py:55-95); build_runtime passes the map to create_deep_agent(interrupt_on=...) (runtime.py:794-798, 929-939); on each HITL interrupt, resolve_interrupts maps the call via tool_to_action to a WRITE Action and calls driver.engine.evaluate, yielding approve/reject/edit decisions (interrupts.py:197, 215-264); rejection records a session deny (interrupts.py:259).
contracts.forbidden_condition: A file-mutating tool call reaching execution without a permission-engine verdict — i.e., a write/edit/wiki-write that runs without engine.evaluate having returned a decision and the corresponding approve/reject/edit resolution being applied.
pending_binding_information: builtin_tools._wire_builtin_tools (which constructs the local write/edit tool instances and returns ungated_tools) is not in the supplied views.
The site that adds wiki_write/wiki_append to extra_tools when wiki is enabled is not supplied (permissions_bridge.py:90-94 states it relies on extra_tools).
contracts.protected_operation: Execution of gated file-mutating agent tool calls (write_file / edit_file / wiki_write / wiki_append).
contracts.protected_resource: Files in the agent's write scope (write/edit targets on the project filesystem; wiki pages for wiki-mutating extras).
contracts.protection_obligation: Every file-mutating agent tool call (write_file, edit_file, and wiki_write/wiki_append when configured as extra tools) must be registered in the deepagents interrupt map and pass a permission-engine decision (ALLOW, approver-answered ASK, or DENY) before it may execute; the tool runs only when the LangGraph graph is resumed with that decision.
scope_limits: Covers only tool names registered in the interrupt map; locally built identity-ungated tools are excluded by object identity (permissions_bridge.py:105-119, runtime.py:787-793).
The content of per-mode decisions (plan/ask/auto-edit/yolo) and danger-guard levels is out of scope here; only the must-be-evaluated-before-execution invariant is asserted.
deepagents/HITL middleware internals (InterruptOnConfig semantics) are known only through jarn call sites.

contracts.commit_point: The sanitize_project call in load_config, applied to project_raw before _deep_merge constructs the merged config (loader.py:333-341).
contracts.declared_mechanism: load_config calls sanitize_project when project_trusted is False, before the merged config is built (loader.py:324-341); sanitize_project keeps only SAFE_PROJECT_KEYS, trims permissions to deny/network.deny, drops allow/sensitive_read_globs, and drops a null deny (trust.py:47-53, 144-183); the allowlist defaults new keys to stripped rather than honoured.
contracts.forbidden_condition: A capability-granting key from an untrusted project tier surviving into the merged effective config — e.g., project-declared hooks or MCP servers activating, project providers pointing base_url at an attacker to exfiltrate secret references, project permission_mode forcing yolo, project permissions.allow pre-approving commands, project network.allow widening egress, or project sensitive_read_globs dropping read protection.
pending_binding_information: The hook-runtime that would execute project-declared hooks (HookRunner construction from config) is not in the supplied views; the binding is established via the documented lifecycle semantics and the pre-tool hook dispatch path.
contracts.protected_operation: Configuration load/merge — load_config building the effective merged Config from the global and project tiers.
contracts.protected_resource: The effective merged Config that wires agent capabilities (lifecycle hooks, MCP tools, providers, permission mode, egress policy, sensitive-read globs).
contracts.protection_obligation: An untrusted project's .jarn/config.yaml must not enable capability-granting settings: at the config-load commit point the project tier is stripped to the SAFE_PROJECT_KEYS allowlist ('ui' plus safety-increasing permissions.deny / network.deny) until the project is explicitly trusted — hooks, mcp_servers, async_subagents, providers, execution, permission_mode, policy, observability, permissions.allow, permissions.network.allow, and permissions.sensitive_read_globs must not take effect.
scope_limits: Global-only keys (gateway) are stripped from every project tier whether trusted or not (loader.py:31-35, 79-93) — outside this trust-conditional contract.
Trusted projects bypass sanitization by design; trust is recorded per root with a fingerprint so gated-key changes re-trigger the prompt (trust.py:27-30, 222-243).
